layer 1 — WAN & the DNS path that exists today

g.text: PPPoE · t-mobile
public 78.80.33.35, no CGNAT → inbound VPN feasible.
MikroTik cloud DDNS is enabled as a second DDNS beside
Cloudflare.
public DNS = the only internal authority
*.hnatekmar.dev records → 172.16.100.15, a private address published publicly.
clients resolve internal names through the internet, then rely on NAT hairpin.
10 dst-nat port-forwards (all enabled)
RB5009UG+S+ · 7.12.1 (upgrade pending)
single bridge, vlan-filtering OFF · all 9 ports pvid=1, admit-all · every port a bridge member
LAN IP 172.16.100.1/24 sits on ether2 (a bridge slave) — the plan flags this as the cut-over risk
ether4 (1 Gb) ↔ CRS326:ether18 · ether5 → 3 MACs, unidentified (AP or small switch) · sfp-sfpplus1 → work subnet 172.16.101.1/24

svg.text: layer 1 — switching: one flat L2 domain, no VLAN entries anywhere

g.text: 24 ports + 2 SFP+, one bridge (vlan-filtering OFF), no bridge VLAN entries
ether18 ↔ RB5009 (1 Gb uplink) · ether4 → CRS804, CSS610 behind it
ether7 → the second 3c:ec:ef box · ether16 → deco-BE22 mesh AP + its clients
two ports are already named by hand: “balteus” (→ PVE host), “bukefalos” (→ TBC)
CRS804-4DDQ · 7.23.3 · .113 RoCE spine
TWO bridges: bridge1 (management, flat with the LAN, via ether1)
bridge-compute = the RDMA fabric — eth2 (TBC) and 4× QSFP-DD at 200G-baseCR4 → spark1..4
the carve must not touch bridge-compute: RoCE/PFC dies at a router
fabric-side addresses are 192.168.0.x — not the 192.168.192.0/24 the plan assumed
no RouterOS API → outside IaC; golden-config, manual changes only
8×1G + 2×SFP+, ports and occupants TBC
decide: give it VLANs from the start, or pin it to VLAN 1 and treat
it as legacy

svg.text: layer 1 — why DNS is the thing that can bite

g.text: what clients are told today
DHCP dhcp1 on bridge hands out 8.8.8.8 as the resolver (10-minute leases) — no internal resolver exists.
/ip/dns has allow-remote-requests = false: the router cannot answer clients even if pointed at it.
static DNS holds only 9 legacy *.dev.hnatekmar.xyz entries; nothing for the current scheme.
so the internal resolution path is: public resolver → public record holding a private IP → hairpin.
the four ways it breaks during the carve
1. wan-restricted on the AI boxes kills their DNS — the local resolver must exist BEFORE egress classes.
2. deny-by-default east-west: a VLAN that cannot reach the VIP .15 resolves names and then fails to connect.
3. .15 floats with the cluster (ARP'd by main-4): wave B moves it, so Cloudflare must move in the same wave.
4. wildcard TLS is DNS-01 via Cloudflare: cut the cluster's egress and renewals fail — on an HSTS-preloaded TLD an expired cert is a hard
failure with no click-through.
mgmt · VLAN 10
switch/AP management, IPMI, one spare
access port per switch first

workstations, phones, AP uplinks — the AP
needs a trunk (SSID→VLAN)

the devops cluster (main-*) and the VIP
.15 move here in wave B

balteus + its keepers, the 3c:ec:ef box,
the NAS
printers/IoT placement to be decided
guest · VLAN 50
WiFi guests via a second SSID; never gets
internal names or the resolver
compat · VLAN 1
172.16.100.0/24 stays until wave C
exits; the RoCE fabric is excluded
entirely
proposed port mechanics
access port (untagged, PVID = the device's class) for single devices; trunk (tagged) for switch uplinks, the router, and the Proxmox
bridge once VM NICs carry VLAN tags.
stage 1 of the IaC touches no ports at all: VLAN interfaces, gateways and address lists only — inert until the bridge becomes
VLAN-filtering.
TBC before this is drawn as fact
whose box is “bukefalos”; what is on CRS326 ether2/5/6/8-15/17/19-22; CRS804 ether2; CSS610 ports and occupants; the MACs on the router's
placeholders are marked TBC on purpose — an invented box is worse than a gap.
